units.title: Design Engineering (H404): 1 Identifying requirements

outcomes.text: Understand that design is context dependent and investigate what makes a context distinct: environment, user requirements, economic and market considerations and product opportunities.
Describe methods for investigating stakeholder needs: user-centred design, SWOT, focus groups, observation and market research.
Explain how enterprise drives new product ideas: entrepreneurship, commercial partnerships, venture capital and crowdfunding.
Analyse user interaction factors: lifestyle impact, ease of use, inclusivity, ergonomics, anthropometric data and aesthetics.
Explain ergonomic factors for engineered products, including anthropometric data, comfort, control layout and software interfaces.

units.title: Design Engineering (H404): 2 Learning from existing products and practice

outcomes.text: Analyse and evaluate existing products for context, materials and components, construction, functionality, ease of use, inclusivity, fitness for purpose, lifestyle impact, trends, marketing and getting to market.
Critically evaluate how new and emerging technologies drive product innovation, including blue sky and incremental innovation.
Explain how past and present engineers and design thinking have influenced products, industry, people and the environment.
Explain how key historical movements and figures influence future developments.
Describe a product's marketing lifecycle from launch to decline, how demand is sustained, and the role of social media.

units.title: Design Engineering (H404): 3 Implications of wider issues

outcomes.text: Explain how social, ethical and environmental issues shape design, including lifecycle assessment, material sources, resource depletion, planned obsolescence, buying trends and environmental directives.
Apply design for manufacture: testing and prototyping, scales of production, repair and maintenance, and product life.
Describe product lifecycle management and engineered lifespans, including compatibility, maintenance, support and end of life.
Explain how environmental factors affect sourcing, waste disposal and cost.
Explain sustainability issues in industrial manufacture: fair trade, ETI, globalisation, recycling, eco-materials and up-cycling.
Explain how to optimise use of materials and components considering cost, stock sizes and sustainable production.
Describe issues in effective and responsible distribution, including cost, environment, social media and global delivery.
Explain intellectual property: registered designs, trademarks, copyright, design rights and patents.
Explain wider issues in selecting energy sources, storage, transmission and use.
Explain the need to draw on mathematics, science and other experts, and to interpret technical data from research.

units.title: Design Engineering (H404): 4 Design thinking and communication

outcomes.text: Use annotated sketching and digital tools to communicate and improve ideas for function, aesthetics, manufacture and materials.
Represent systems and components with working drawings, digital visualisations, circuit and system diagrams, flowcharts, prototypes and models.
Explain how designers use digital tools and online collaboration to develop products.
Explain how CAD and CAE support rendering, simulation and scientific analysis of real-world factors.
Describe approaches to exploring and evaluating ideas: iterative design, user-centred design, circular economy and systems thinking.
Explain the importance of collaboration across subject areas.
Describe system design through user-interface, data and process design.
Describe project management approaches such as critical path analysis, scrum and six sigma.

units.title: Design Engineering (H404): 5 Material and component considerations

outcomes.text: Explain the factors influencing selection of materials and components: performance, aesthetics, cost, properties, environment and ethics.
Distinguish metals, polymers, timbers and boards, textiles, composites, smart and modern materials and their uses.
Describe material properties such as density, tensile strength, hardness, conductivity, corrosion resistance, elasticity and machinability.
Explain how available forms, costs and properties affect material suitability.

units.title: Design Engineering (H404): 6 Technical understanding

outcomes.text: Explain why materials and components are reinforced or stiffened, using triangulation and reinforcing.
Describe mechanical devices providing rotary, linear, reciprocating and oscillating motion.
Describe devices that change the magnitude and direction of forces and torques: gears, cams, pulleys, levers, linkages, screws, chains and belts.
Describe epicyclic gears, bearings, lubrication and efficiency.
Describe static and dynamic forces and rigidity: tension, compression, torsion, bending, stress, strain, elasticity, mass, weight and failure modes.
Explain how electronic systems provide input, control and output: switches, sensors, programmable devices, amplification and output devices.
Describe system parts: passive components, input sensors, microcontrollers, MOSFET and driver ICs, outputs, analogue and digital signals, open and closed loops, and sub-systems.
Explain interfacing electronics with mechanical and pneumatic systems.
Describe networking and protocols: RFID, NFC, Wi-Fi, bluetooth, embedded devices and smart objects.
Explain voltage, current, Ohm's law and power.
Explain how smart materials change product functionality.
Explain how programmable devices add functionality, including measuring, controlling, storing and displaying data, prototyping platforms and IDEs, and flowcharts for control.

units.title: Design Engineering (H404): 7 Manufacturing processes and techniques

outcomes.text: Make 3D iterative models and working prototypes from various materials, using hand tools and digital tools.
Select and safely use workshop tools for subtractive, additive and deforming processes.
Explain CAM and CAE, including 3D printing and subtractive CNC cutting, milling, turning and routing.
Explain measuring instruments and techniques to ensure accuracy and tolerances.
Explain how forms, costs and working properties affect material suitability.
Describe polymer moulding, metal casting and sheet metal forming methods.
Describe industrial electronics assembly: surface mount technology and PCB assembly.
Explain the benefits of computer-controlled machinery, automated handling and robot arms.
Explain how manufacturers optimise use of materials and production for cost effectiveness.

topics.title: 7.4 and 7.5 Scales of production and quality

outcomes.text: Explain one-off, batch and high volume production, modular and cell systems, lean, just-in-time and fully automated manufacture.
Explain how ICT and digital technologies change manufacturing: customisation, rapid prototyping, additive manufacture and stock control.
Explain quality control, quality assurance, Total Quality Management and European and British standards.

units.title: Design Engineering (H404): 8 Viability of design solutions

outcomes.text: Evaluate whether a solution meets functionality, ease of use, inclusivity and user needs.
Explain testing with stakeholders throughout development.
Explain testing the feasibility of getting a product to market, including cost, packaging and appeal.
Explain the relevant BSI and ISO standards.

topics.title: 8.2 and 8.3 Technical testing and commercial viability

outcomes.text: Explain physical testing of functionality, accuracy and performance.
Describe destructive and non-destructive testing, durability testing, prototype testing, consumer and virtual testing.
Explain feasibility studies and factors in commercial viability: lifestyle impact, performance, manufacture difficulty, stock, cost and profit, timescales, branding and market analysis.

units.title: Design Engineering (H404): 9 Health and safety

outcomes.text: Explain safe workshop practice: risk assessments, hazards and control measures.
Explain safe use of specialist tools, processes and machinery.
Explain the Health and Safety at Work Act, COSHH, PPE regulations and machinery maintenance.
Explain manufacturers' duty to label products and offer warranties for safety assurance.

Explain how environmental factors affect sourcing, waste disposal and cost.
Explain sustainability in industrial manufacture: fair trade, ETI, globalisation, recycling, eco-materials and up-cycling.

units.title: Fashion and Textiles (H405): 4 Design thinking and communication

outcomes.text: Use annotated sketching and digital tools to communicate and improve ideas.
Communicate construction with technical drawings, digital visualisations, pattern drafting with cutting and construction symbols, lay plans, prototypes and toiles.

topics.title: 4.2 and 4.3 Digital tools and design thinking

outcomes.text: Explain how designers use digital tools, online collaboration, rendering and simulation.
Describe design approaches: iterative design, user-centred design, circular economy and systems thinking.
Explain the importance of cross-subject collaboration.
Describe project management approaches such as critical path analysis, scrum and six sigma.

units.title: Fashion and Textiles (H405): 5 Material considerations

outcomes.text: Explain the factors influencing the selection of materials: performance, aesthetics, cost, properties, environment and ethics.
Distinguish natural and synthetic textiles, blends, and metals, wood and rubber used in component parts.
Classify textile fibres by source: natural animal, plant and mineral, and synthetic.
Classify yarns: single fibre, mixed and blended, filament, fancy, bulked and textured.
Classify fabric structures: knitted, structured, woven, non-woven and microfibres.
Explain how properties such as strength, softness, durability, elasticity, flammability, absorbency, washability and breathability make fibres, yarns and fabrics suitable for products.
Explain how available forms, costs and properties affect material suitability.

units.title: Fashion and Textiles (H405): 6 Technical understanding

outcomes.text: Explain why materials need reinforcing or stiffening for structural integrity.
Explain constructional solutions: whole garment knitting versus fully fashioned panels, boning, darts, gathers, elastic, pleats and quilting.
Explain functional, decorative and constructional components such as fastenings, trims and interfacing.
Describe printing and dyeing techniques, biological finishes such as enzyme stone wash, embroidery, applique, mechanical and digital techniques.
Describe finishes preventing decay or enhancing performance: laminating, water repellence, stain, flame and moth-proofing, breathable and transparent coatings.
Explain smart materials: thermochromic, photochromic and electrochromic fibres, shape memory alloy and breathable membranes.
Explain e-textiles, conductive threads and pigments, fibretronics and programmable controllers with sensors.
Explain technical textiles, such as geotextiles and hi-tech clothing fabrics.

units.title: Fashion and Textiles (H405): 7 Manufacturing processes and techniques

outcomes.text: Make iterative models such as samples and toiles using pattern making and drafting to test fit and structure.
Use hand and digital tools, rapid prototyping and simulation for iterative development.
Recognise the order of assembly for fashion and textiles products.
Use tools, processes and machinery for dyeing, printing, marking, cutting, joining and finishing.
Explain how CAD and CAM, templates and patterns support accurate final prototypes.
Explain pattern cutting: sizing, symbols and instructions, and manipulating patterns.
Recognise industrial tools and machinery for dyeing, printing, marking, cutting, joining and finishing textiles.
Explain how manufacturers optimise materials and production through economical lay plans and costing, and efficient use of labour and capital.

topics.title: 7.4 and 7.5 Scales of production and quality

outcomes.text: Explain one-off, batch and high volume, modular and cell, lean, just-in-time, bought-in parts and fully automated production.
Explain how ICT and digital technologies change manufacturing.
Explain quality control, quality assurance, Total Quality Management and European and British standards.

units.title: Fashion and Textiles (H405): 8 Viability of design solutions

outcomes.text: Evaluate whether a solution meets functionality, ease of use, inclusivity and user needs, with stakeholder testing and market feasibility.
Explain BSI and ISO standards relevant to the subject.
Explain physical testing of functionality, accuracy and performance, including fibre and fabric durability and aftercare testing, prototype and toile testing, wearer trials and virtual testing.
Explain feasibility studies and factors in commercial viability.

units.title: Fashion and Textiles (H405): 9 Health and safety

outcomes.text: Explain safe workshop practice: risk assessments, hazards and control measures, and safe use of specialist tools and machinery.
Explain the Health and Safety at Work Act, COSHH and PPE regulations.
Explain manufacturers' duty to label and guarantee products, including care labelling and flammability.
